S054-01.notes: 'Avoiding dramatic language and acknowledging the arguments on every side' defines 'measured'; the 'Though...bold' contrast confirms it. 'Exhaustive' is the best trap because of 'every side', but it describes coverage, not tone, and doesn't contrast with 'bold'. 'Partisan' contradicts the passage, and nothing supports 'belated'.

S054-02.notes: The pill was the same and inactive, and the groups were randomly assigned, so the warning (expectation) is the only difference. B is ruled out by 'inactive', D by random assignment, and C is an overreaching policy claim. The nocebo framing is accurate.

S054-03.notes: 4% of 200,000 = 8,000 and 6% of 300,000 = 18,000, so the number grew 2.25 times (more than doubled), while the share went from 4% to 6% (a rise of half). Only D supports both parts of the claim. C gives only the 2023 count, A only the share, and B only the workforce.

S054-04.notes: The final sentence states the main idea. A is the old view the text revises, C overgeneralizes one finding, and D distorts a detail. The historiographic framing (older monopoly view vs. recent mixed view, e.g., Ogilvie vs. Epstein) is accurate enough.

S054-05.notes: The relative pronoun is the object of 'hired' ('the library hired whom'), so 'whom' is correct. 'Who' is the common trap. 'Whose' would need a noun after it, and 'which' isn't used for people in this context. Inserting each option gives no other grammatical sentence.

S054-06.notes: In an inverted past counterfactual, 'Had + past participle' gives 'Had the engineers examined', which pairs with 'would have noticed'. 'Had...have examined' and 'Had...examine/examines' are ungrammatical. Note that 'examined' is both the past form and the past participle, so a student can get it right without fully understanding the structure.

flags.note: Choice B says colonies 'unable to read it' (the dance), but the notes say they were prevented only from reading dance DIRECTIONS. This is a slight overstatement in the keyed answer. Consider 'unable to read its directions'.

S054-07.notes: B is the only choice that presents the counterintuitive result: the dance signals food, yet colonies that couldn't read it did about as well in some seasons. C is the expected finding, A is background, and D describes the method without the result. The facts check out: von Frisch decoded the dance in the 1940s (Nobel Prize 1973), and disoriented-dance studies (e.g., Sherman & Visscher 2002) found that the benefit depended on season.

S054-08.notes: Text 2 proposes signaling to insects (the coevolution/aphid hypothesis of Hamilton & Brown and Archetti) as an alternative to the photoprotection hypothesis. B is too absolute, since Text 2 never denies the sunscreen effect. In C the ecologists explain the regional pattern by insects, not sunlight. D is unsupported. Both hypotheses are described accurately.
